messages:
Jamie O.: quick spike idea — propose a small 'trace-muxer' layer that shards traces to different vendor adapters. primary rules: keep trace coherence (all spans for a trace to same backend) but allow rule-based routing for high-signal traces to honeycomb/datadog and bulk lower-cost traces to tempo/splunk. want thoughts before i write an RFC
Liam P.: how do you plan to ensure all spans for a trace land in the same backend? hashing trace_id?
Jamie O.: yeah, two-tier approach: 1) route by explicit attribute (service, telemetry.route, env) 2) fallback to hash(trace_id) % N where N is number of adapter slots for that route. that keeps spans together while allowing controlled split across vendors
Maria (observability): important: Tempo/Jaeger expect full traces for the timeline UI. if we split spans across vendors, trace view will be broken. so rule: when routing to tempo/jaeger, all spans for that trace must go to the same tempo cluster.
Ravi S.: also watch duplication — if we ever fanout to multiple vendors we double/triple bytes. costs blow up. prefer selective fanout only for traces flagged as 'high-signal' by sampling or an enrichment pipeline.
Eve (infra): +1 on cost concern. we need per-vendor quotas and backpressure: if splunk ingestion is saturated, muxer should fallback traces to a buffered local store and mark them for async replay or route to tempo as degraded path.
Jamie O.: agree. sketch of policy grammar i was thinking:
```yaml
rules:
  - match: service =~ "^payments-.*"
    route: honeycomb
    sampling: 1.0
  - match: env == "prod" and trace.duration_ms > 500
    route: datadog
    sampling: 0.1
  - default:
    route: tempo_pool
    sampling: 0.02
```
Maria (observability): that looks good. also add an attribute-preservation rule: ensure trace_id is kept, and add vendor_marker span tag so we can detect cross-vendor artifacts. for honeycomb we might want to push additional context fields (build, commit).
Liam P.: how will this interact with upstream sampling decisions? if client SDK set sampled=false we shouldn't force route to high-cost vendors unless explicitly overridden. maybe honor upstream sampling headers unless rule has override flag.
Ravi S.: +1. also: hashing modulo buckets only works if bucket count is stable. bucket resizing causes re-sharding and split traces. need consistent hashing (jump hash or rendezvous) so reconfig doesn't move a lot of traces.
Eve (infra): and we need observability for the muxer itself: per-route inflight, dropped_by_quota, retry_queue_depth, last_replay_time. console should expose these and estimated monthly cost by route so product can reason about spend.
Maria (observability): for vendor differences: Honeycomb prefers event-based ingestion (you can reconstruct traces but it's expensive), Datadog wants traces and spans with certain field shapes, Tempo wants raw spans. adapters need small transform steps, but we should avoid heavy transformation in the hot path. use lightweight adapters and a separate enrichment worker for heavyweight mapping.
Jamie O.: good call. thinking implementation tiers:
- hot path: route decision + minimal transform + adapter send (sync-ish with retry)
- offline enrich: long-running worker for extra attributes and backfill
- replay: durable queue (SQS/kafka) for traces rejected by vendor due to quota/backpressure

DeployBot: deploy started: trace-muxer/alpha -> canary (5% traffic) by Jamie O.
Ravi S.: canary sounds right. for the canary route we should pin a small set of services and also verify trace continuity in tempo and honeycomb by running a check job that queries both and compares trace_ids for a sample.
Maria (observability): i'll add a canary test to the monitoring workbook: sample 100 traces per minute, confirm 100% span coverage in backend. alert if < 98% coverage or if end-to-end latency spikes > 200ms.
Liam P.: UX note: console rollout page should let ops toggle per-service routing rules and show immediate impact estimates (qps, expected downstream cost delta). saves us from a tty-only rollout.
Eve (infra): also need RBAC — only SRE/obs can change global routing rules; product/teams can have per-service overrides with caps.
Jamie O.: next steps: i'll draft RFC with architecture, consistent-hashing plan, quota/fallback strategy, and adapter shim spec. will include a sample rule grammar and canary plan. volunteers for review?
Maria (observability): i'll review and add monitoring checks
Ravi S.: i'll review for cost/backpressure paths
Liam P.: i'll review the hashing/consistency parts
Eve (infra): i'll look at replay durability and RBAC enforcement
DeployBot: deploy succeeded: trace-muxer/alpha -> canary (5%) :white_check_mark:
Jamie O.: thanks all — filing RFC now (link forthcoming) :rocket:
